headline: The head of the International Monetary Fund says heavy spending on AI is keeping world growth near 3% despite an energy shock, and could lift Asian economies.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: the Reuters wire story was read in full and matches the headline, but the growth figures are the IMF chief's own estimates ahead of the Fund's updated forecast on Tuesday.
importance_line: What changed is that the head of the IMF credits AI investment with holding world growth near 3% while warning about jobs and taxes, which matters first to workers and households in Asia and elsewhere, then to governments and IMF members, then to the Asian hardware makers that supply the build-out, and the doubt is that the growth effects are her estimates, not yet in an IMF forecast.
summary: Reuters reports that IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva told the opening of the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok on Monday 12 Oct 2026 that strong investment in AI infrastructure is keeping global growth at about 3% despite the energy supply shock, and could add half to one full percentage point to growth in advanced Asian economies and 0.2 to 0.8 points in emerging ones. She also called AI a "slow-moving tsunami" for jobs, education and tax revenue, said the IMF estimates 40% of jobs could be augmented, downgraded or eliminated over time, and noted the Fund publishes an updated world outlook on Tuesday.
notes: Reuters page returned HTTP 401; the Reuters wire text was read in Yahoo Finance's copy. Link kept to the Reuters original.
